_about: Sin, exile and death side by side (plan 7.6b): wordings of sin, exile and death that more than one book shares, from Genesis and the history books to the psalms, the prophets and the letters, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: Sin desires you: let it not rule

The Law & history: sin is crouching at your door; it desires you, but you must master it
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 19:13
Keep Your servant also from willful sins; may they not rule over me
Psalm 119:133
let no sin rule over me
The letters: do not let sin reign in your mortal body so that you obey its desires
For sin shall not be your master

rows.alike: Each speaks of sin as something that would rule a person: it "desires you" (Genesis 4:7), "may they not rule over me" (Psalm 19:13), "let no sin rule over me" (Psalm 119:133), "do not let sin reign" (Romans 6:12), "sin shall not be your master" (Romans 6:14).
rows.different: Genesis 4:7 is said to one who may "do what is right" or "refuse to do what is right", and ends "you must master it"; Psalm 19:13 and Psalm 119:133 speak to "You" in the first person ("Keep Your servant", "Order my steps in Your word"); Romans 6:12 and 6:14 say "do not let sin reign in your mortal body" and "sin shall not be your master".

rows.title: Evil in the heart

The Law & history: every inclination of the thoughts of his heart was altogether evil all the time
every inclination of his heart is evil from his youth
Psalms & wisdom: Ecclesiastes 9:3
the hearts of men are full of evil and madness while they are alive
Ecclesiastes 8:11
the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil
The Prophets: The heart is deceitful above all things and beyond cure. Who can understand it?
each of you follows the stubbornness of his evil heart instead of obeying Me
each of us will act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart
Gospels & Acts: For from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts
For out of the heart come evil thoughts
The letters: a wicked heart of unbelief that turns away from the living God

rows.alike: Each speaks of the heart as evil, deceitful or darkened: "every inclination of his heart is evil" (Genesis 8:21), "the hearts of men are full of evil" (Ecclesiastes 9:3), "the hearts of men become fully set on doing evil" (Ecclesiastes 8:11), "The heart is deceitful above all things" (Jeremiah 17:9), "his evil heart" (Jeremiah 16:12), "from within the hearts of men come evil thoughts" (Mark 7:21), "darkened in their foolish hearts" (Romans 1:21).
rows.different: Genesis 6:5 says what "the LORD saw", "all the time", and 8:21 what He "said in His heart"; Ecclesiastes 8:11 begins "When the sentence for a crime is not speedily executed"; Jeremiah 16:12 says "each of you follows the stubbornness of his evil heart instead of obeying Me", and 18:12 is what "they will reply", "each of us will act according to the stubbornness of his evil heart"; Jeremiah 17:9 asks "Who can understand it?"; Hebrews warns "none of you" to have "a wicked heart of unbelief".

rows.title: A stiff-necked people

The Law & history: they are indeed a stiff-necked people
Although this is a stiff-necked people, forgive our iniquity and sin
for you are a stiff-necked people
For I know how rebellious and stiff-necked you are
they stiffened their necks like their fathers
do not stiffen your necks as your fathers did
But they and our fathers became arrogant and stiff-necked
they are indeed a stiff-necked people
they stiffened their necks and would not obey
Psalms & wisdom: Proverbs 29:1
A man who remains stiff-necked after much reproof will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery
The Prophets: they stiffened their necks and did more evil than their fathers
they stiffened their necks and would not listen or receive My discipline
because they have stiffened their necks so as not to heed My words

rows.alike: The same words recur of a people: "a stiff-necked people" (Exodus 32:9; 33:3; Deuteronomy 9:6; 9:13), "they stiffened their necks" (2 Kings 17:14; Nehemiah 9:29; Jeremiah 7:26), "You stiff-necked people" (Acts 7:51); several add the fathers, "as your fathers did" (2 Chronicles 30:8).
rows.different: In Exodus 32:9 the LORD says it to Moses; in Exodus 34:9 it is part of a plea, "forgive our iniquity and sin"; Proverbs 29:1 says it of "A man" who "will suddenly be shattered beyond recovery"; in Acts 7:51 it is said to those addressed, who "always resist the Holy Spirit, just as your fathers did".

rows.title: They rebelled against Me

The Law & history: Only do not rebel against the LORD
because both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah
you have been rebelling against the LORD
You have been rebelling against the LORD since the day I came to know you
But they were disobedient and rebelled against You
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 107:11
because they rebelled against the words of God
The Prophets: I have raised children and brought them up, but they have rebelled against Me
a rebellious nation that has rebelled against Me
The LORD is righteous, yet I rebelled against His command
We have sinned and rebelled; You have not forgiven
even though we have rebelled against Him
The letters: For who were the ones who heard and rebelled?

rows.alike: The same word, "rebelled", is used of rebelling against God and His word: "they have rebelled against Me" (Isaiah 1:2), "has rebelled against Me" (Ezekiel 2:3), "rebelled against You" (Nehemiah 9:26), "rebelled against the words of God" (Psalm 107:11), "heard and rebelled" (Hebrews 3:16).
rows.different: Numbers 20:24 says it of Aaron and of the one spoken to, "both of you"; in Isaiah 1:2 the speaker says "I have raised children"; Lamentations 1:18 ("yet I rebelled against His command") and Daniel 9:9 ("we have rebelled against Him") are in the first person; Hebrews 3:16 asks it of "all those Moses led out of Egypt".

rows.title: They have forsaken Me and served other gods

The Law & history: But you have forsaken Me and served other gods
we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and Ashtoreths
Because they have forsaken the LORD their God who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods
Because they have forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt, and have embraced other gods
because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods
because they have forsaken Me and burned incense to other gods
they have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians
you have forsaken the commandments of the LORD and have followed the Baals
Jehoram had forsaken the LORD, the God of his fathers
Because you have forsaken the LORD, He has forsaken you
Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers
they had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers
The Prophets: They have forsaken the LORD; they have despised the Holy One of Israel
because they have forsaken Me, and they have burned incense to other gods
They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living water
Just as you have forsaken Me and served foreign gods in your land, so will you serve foreigners in a land that is not your own
your fathers have forsaken Me, declares the LORD, and followed other gods
they have abandoned the LORD, the fountain of living water
Your children have forsaken Me and sworn by gods that are not gods
You have forsaken Me, declares the LORD
burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods
they have forsaken the covenant of the LORD their God and have worshiped and served other gods
stop burning incense to other gods
burning incense to other gods in the land of Egypt

rows.alike: The same pair of charges recurs: "forsaken Me" and "other gods" (Judges 10:13; 2 Kings 22:17; Jeremiah 1:16; Jeremiah 16:11), and in Kings and Chronicles the same answer to why disaster came, "Because they have forsaken the LORD ... and have embraced other gods" (1 Kings 9:9; 2 Chronicles 7:22). The same charges are also made singly or together: "they have forsaken Me to worship Ashtoreth" (1 Kings 11:33), "You have forsaken Me" (2 Chronicles 12:5; Jeremiah 15:6), "Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers" (2 Chronicles 24:24), "burning incense to other gods" (Jeremiah 44:8; 44:15).
rows.different: 1 Samuel 12:10 is the people's own confession; Jeremiah 2:13 and 17:13 call the LORD "the fountain of living water"; Jeremiah 5:19 sets serving "foreign gods in your land" beside serving "foreigners in a land that is not your own"; 2 Chronicles 12:5 and 24:20 answer it, "I have forsaken you" and "He has forsaken you"; Jeremiah 5:7 says "gods that are not gods".

rows.title: They provoked His jealousy

The Law & history: They provoked His jealousy with foreign gods
They have provoked My jealousy by that which is not God
by the sins they committed they provoked Him to jealous anger more than all their fathers had done
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 78:58
provoked His jealousy with their idols
The Prophets: the idol that provokes jealousy was seated
The letters: Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy?
I will make you jealous by those who are not a nation
in the hope that I may provoke my own people to jealousy

rows.alike: Each speaks of provoking jealousy, with "foreign gods" (Deuteronomy 32:16), "their idols" (Psalm 78:58), "the idol that provokes jealousy" (Ezekiel 8:3), and asks "Are we trying to provoke the Lord to jealousy?" (1 Corinthians 10:22).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 32:21 is in the first person, "They have provoked My jealousy by that which is not God"; 1 Kings 14:22 says Judah "provoked Him to jealous anger more than all their fathers had done"; in Ezekiel 8:3 the speaker is carried "in visions of God to Jerusalem, to the entrance of the north gate of the inner court", where the idol "was seated"; 1 Corinthians 10:22 goes on "Are we stronger than He?". Romans 10:19, 11:11 and 11:14 use the words of making Israel jealous, another subject.

rows.title: Evil in the sight of the LORD

The Law & history: And the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD and served the Baals
So the Israelites did evil in the sight of the LORD; they forgot the LORD their God
So Solomon did evil in the sight of the LORD
They devoted themselves to doing evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger
And he did evil in the sight of the LORD by following the abominations of the nations
And Zedekiah did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 51:4
Against You, You only, have I sinned and done what is evil in Your sight
The Prophets: you did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight
But they did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight
For the people of Judah have done evil in My sight, declares the LORD
And Zedekiah did evil in the sight of the LORD, just as Jehoiakim had done

rows.alike: The same phrase is used of Israel, of Solomon and of Zedekiah: "did evil in the sight of the LORD" (Judges 2:11; 1 Kings 11:6; 2 Kings 24:19); close wording is used in "done what is evil in Your sight" (Psalm 51:4) and "you did evil in My sight" (Isaiah 65:12).
rows.different: In Judges 2:11, 1 Kings 11:6 and 2 Kings 24:19 it is told of others; in Psalm 51:4 the speaker says it of himself, "Against You, You only, have I sinned"; in Isaiah 65:12, 66:4 and Jeremiah 7:30 it is said in the first person, "in My sight" (Jeremiah 7:30 adds "declares the LORD"). 2 Kings 24:19 and Jeremiah 52:2 are word for word the same.

rows.title: We have sinned; I have sinned

The Law & history: We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly
We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly
We have sinned against You, for we have indeed forsaken our God
We have sinned against the LORD
Both I and my father's house have sinned
I have sinned against the LORD your God and against you
I have sinned against the LORD, the God of Israel
I have sinned; I have transgressed the LORD's commandment and your instructions
I have sinned against the LORD
I have sinned greatly in what I have done
We have sinned by speaking against the LORD and against you
We have sinned against the LORD
We have sinned, for we have forsaken the LORD and served the Baals and Ashtoreths
your servant knows that I have sinned
I, the shepherd, have sinned and acted wickedly
I have sinned greatly because I have done this thing
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 106:6
We have sinned like our fathers; we have done wrong and acted wickedly
Psalm 41:4
heal me, for I have sinned against You
I have sinned and perverted what was right
Psalms 51:4
Against You, You only, have I sinned
The Prophets: we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly and rebelled
We have sinned against the LORD our God, both we and our fathers
We acknowledge our wickedness, O LORD, the guilt of our fathers; indeed, we have sinned against You
Because I have sinned against Him, I must endure the rage of the LORD
we have sinned against the LORD
we have sinned; we have acted wickedly
Gospels & Acts: Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you
Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you
I have sinned by betraying innocent blood

rows.alike: The same words of confession, "We have sinned" and "I have sinned", and one fuller form: "We have sinned and done wrong; we have acted wickedly" (1 Kings 8:47; 2 Chronicles 6:37), with small changes in "We have sinned like our fathers; we have done wrong and acted wickedly" (Psalm 106:6) and "we have sinned and done wrong. We have acted wickedly" (Daniel 9:5). The short forms recur: "I have sinned" (Exodus 9:27; Numbers 22:34; 1 Samuel 15:30) and "We have sinned" (Numbers 21:7; Judges 10:15; Lamentations 3:42); Daniel 9:15 has "we have sinned; we have acted wickedly".
rows.different: The speakers differ: Pharaoh (Exodus 10:16), Achan (Joshua 7:20), Saul (1 Samuel 15:24), David (2 Samuel 12:13), those who "confessed" at Mizpah (1 Samuel 7:6), a prayer for "the Israelites" in which "Both I and my father's house have sinned" (Nehemiah 1:6), one who says "I have sinned by betraying innocent blood" (Matthew 27:4), and a son who says "Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you" (Luke 15:18; 15:21). Psalm 106:6 and Jeremiah 3:25 and 14:20 add "our fathers". Balaam says it to "the angel of the LORD" (Numbers 22:34), and Psalm 51:4 says "Against You, You only, have I sinned".

rows.title: Who can say, ‘I have kept my heart pure’? All have sinned

Psalms & wisdom: Proverbs 20:9
I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin
What is man, that he should be pure, or one born of woman, that he should be righteous?
Job 25:4
How then can a man be just before God? How can one born of woman be pure?
The letters: If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves
If we say we have not sinned, we make Him out to be a liar
for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God
Jews and Greeks alike are all under sin
the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin

rows.alike: Each speaks of sin as reaching everyone, or of no one being able to claim to be pure: "Who can say, 'I have kept my heart pure; I am cleansed from my sin'?" (Proverbs 20:9), "How can one born of woman be pure?" (Job 25:4), "If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves" (1 John 1:8), "all have sinned" (Romans 3:23), "all things confined by sin" (Galatians 3:22).
rows.different: Proverbs 20:9, Job 15:14 and Job 25:4 are put as questions; 1 John 1:8 and 1:10 put it as "If we say"; Romans 3:23 states "all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God" and 3:9 names "Jews and Greeks alike"; Galatians 3:22 says "the Scripture pronounces all things confined by sin".

rows.title: Like sheep gone astray

Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 119:176
I have strayed like a lost sheep; seek Your servant
The Prophets: We all like sheep have gone astray, each one has turned to his own way
My people are lost sheep; their shepherds have led them astray
My flock went astray on all the mountains and every high hill
Gospels & Acts: If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray
The letters: you were like sheep going astray

rows.alike: Each speaks of sheep going astray: "I have strayed like a lost sheep" (Psalm 119:176), "We all like sheep have gone astray" (Isaiah 53:6), "My flock went astray" (Ezekiel 34:6), "one of them goes astray" (Matthew 18:12), "you were like sheep going astray" (1 Peter 2:25).
rows.different: Psalm 119:176 is in the first person and asks "seek Your servant"; Isaiah 53:6 says "We all" and goes on "each one has turned to his own way"; Jeremiah 50:6 says "their shepherds have led them astray"; Ezekiel 34:6 says they were "scattered over the face of all the earth, with no one to search for them or seek them out"; Matthew 18:12 puts it as a question, "If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray"; 1 Peter 2:25 continues "but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls".

rows.title: Adam, and death through a man

The Law & history: So Adam lived a total of 930 years, and then he died
The letters: just as sin entered the world through one man, and death through sin, so also death was passed on to all men, because all sinned
death reigned from Adam until Moses, even over those who did not sin in the way that Adam transgressed
For since death came through a man
For as in Adam all die

rows.alike: Genesis records of Adam "and then he died"; Romans and 1 Corinthians name Adam, or "one man", with death: "death reigned from Adam" (Romans 5:14), "in Adam all die" (1 Corinthians 15:22).
rows.different: Genesis gives Adam's years and his death; Romans 5:12 speaks of sin and death entering "through one man" and of death passed "to all men, because all sinned"; 1 Corinthians 15:21-22 speaks of death "through a man" and "in Adam".

rows.title: The serpent deceived

The Law & history: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field
The letters: Eve was deceived by the serpent's cunning
it was not Adam who was deceived, but the woman who was deceived and fell into transgression

rows.alike: Each speaks of the serpent's craft or of deceiving: "more crafty" (Genesis 3:1), "The serpent deceived me" (Genesis 3:13), "Eve was deceived by the serpent's cunning" (2 Corinthians 11:3), "the woman who was deceived" (1 Timothy 2:14).
rows.different: In Genesis the woman says it to the LORD God, "and I ate"; 2 Corinthians uses it of a fear that "your minds may be led astray"; 1 Timothy sets "not Adam" beside "the woman".

rows.title: Naked, and the shame of it

The Law & history: And the man and his wife were both naked, and they were not ashamed
they knew that they were naked; so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves
I was afraid because I was naked; so I hid myself
The Prophets: Your nakedness will be uncovered and your shame will be exposed
Jerusalem has sinned greatly; therefore she has become an object of scorn. All who honored her now despise her, for they have seen her nakedness
and they will see you completely naked
I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms
Revelation: wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked
white garments so that you may be clothed and your shameful nakedness not exposed
so that he will not go naked and let his shame be exposed

rows.alike: Each joins nakedness to shame, fear or covering it: "naked, and they were not ashamed" (Genesis 2:25), "so I hid myself" (Genesis 3:10), "Your nakedness will be uncovered and your shame will be exposed" (Isaiah 47:3), "your shameful nakedness not exposed" (Revelation 3:18).
rows.different: Genesis tells it of "the man and his wife"; Isaiah 47:3 goes on "I will take vengeance; I will spare no one"; Lamentations 1:8 says it after "Jerusalem has sinned greatly"; Ezekiel 16:37 says "they will see you completely naked" and Nahum 3:5 "I will show your nakedness to the nations"; Revelation 3:17-18 sets "I am rich" beside "wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked" and counsels "white garments", and 16:15 says "Blessed is the one who remains awake and clothed".

rows.title: Thorns and thistles, and the cursed ground

The Law & history: Both thorns and thistles it will yield for you
the ground that the LORD has cursed
The Prophets: it is the sin of Israel; thorns and thistles will overgrow their altars
Gospels & Acts: Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?
The letters: But land that produces thorns and thistles is worthless, and its curse is imminent

rows.alike: In all three "thorns and thistles" are named: "it will yield for you" (Genesis 3:18), "will overgrow their altars" (Hosea 10:8), "land that produces thorns and thistles" (Hebrews 6:8); Genesis 5:29 speaks of "the ground that the LORD has cursed" and Hebrews 6:8 of land whose "curse is imminent".
rows.different: Genesis 3:18 is said in the second person, "for you", and goes on "you will eat the plants of the field"; Hosea 10:8 sets it with the high places of Aven, "it is the sin of Israel"; Hebrews 6:8 adds "is worthless" and "In the end it will be burned". Matthew 7:16 uses thistles of knowing people by their fruit, another subject; Isaiah 10:17 has a fire "devour Assyria's thorns and thistles", also another subject.

rows.title: You will surely die

The Law & history: for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die
be aware that you will surely die-you and all who belong to you
the LORD had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness
because by this deed you have shown utter contempt for the word of the LORD, the son born to you will surely die
The Prophets: Since he has committed all these abominations, he will surely die

rows.alike: The same words of a death sentence, "you will surely die", are given for a deed: eating from the tree (Genesis 2:17), not restoring a man's wife (Genesis 20:7), "this deed" (2 Samuel 12:14), "all these abominations" (Ezekiel 18:13); it is said to Ahimelech (1 Samuel 22:16) and, as what "the LORD says", to King Ahaziah (2 Kings 1:6; 1:16).
rows.different: The serpent denies it, "You will not surely die" (Genesis 3:4); in Ezekiel 33:14 the sentence is followed by "and he turns from his sin and does what is just and right"; in Jeremiah 26:8 "the priests and prophets and all the people" seize one who had "finished telling all the people everything the LORD had commanded him to say" and shout "You must surely die!"; in Ezekiel 3:18 and 33:8 it is a case, "If I say to the wicked man", and the one who does not warn is held "responsible for his blood" (3:18) or "accountable for his blood" (33:8).

rows.title: He will die in his iniquity; you will die in your sins

The Law & history: Instead, he died because of his own sin
The Prophets: that wicked man will die in his iniquity
he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved yourself
If you did not warn him, he will die in his sin
that one will be taken away in his iniquity
then that wicked man will die in his iniquity
he will die in his iniquity, but you will have saved your life
Because of the unfaithfulness and sin he has committed, he will die
He will die because of the iniquity he has committed
Gospels & Acts: but you will die in your sin
That is why I told you that you would die in your sins

rows.alike: The same words, dying "in" or "because of" one's own sin: "he will die in his iniquity" (Ezekiel 3:19), "he will die in his sin" (Ezekiel 3:20), "he died because of his own sin" (Numbers 27:3), "you will die in your sin" (John 8:21).
rows.different: Numbers 27:3 is said of "Our father", who "was not among the followers of Korah"; Ezekiel 3:18-20 speaks of "a wicked man" and of "a righteous man" who "turns from his righteousness", and 33:6 of "the watchman"; John 8:21 has "I am going away, and you will look for Me", and 8:24 "For unless you believe that I am He, you will die in your sins".

rows.title: The soul who sins is the one who will die; the wages of sin is death

Psalms & wisdom: Proverbs 11:19
Genuine righteousness leads to life, but the pursuit of evil brings death
The Prophets: The soul who sins is the one who will die
The letters: The outcome of those things is death
For the wages of sin is death
it produced death in me through what was good
the law of sin and death
The sting of death is sin, and the power of sin is the law
and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death

rows.alike: Each joins sin, or evil, to death: "the pursuit of evil brings death" (Proverbs 11:19), "The soul who sins is the one who will die" (Ezekiel 18:4), "the wages of sin is death" (Romans 6:23), "sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death" (James 1:15).
rows.different: Ezekiel 18:4 adds "every soul belongs to Me; both father and son are Mine"; Proverbs 11:19 and Romans 6:23 each set death beside life, "righteousness leads to life" and "the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord"; Romans 7:13 says "it produced death in me through what was good"; 1 Corinthians 15:56 adds "the power of sin is the law".

rows.title: Dead, and alive

Gospels & Acts: For this son of mine was dead and is alive again!
this brother of yours was dead and is alive again
he has crossed over from death to life
The letters: And you were dead in your trespasses and sins
made us alive with Christ even when we were dead in our trespasses
When you were dead in your trespasses and in the uncircumcision of your sinful nature, God made you alive with Christ
count yourselves dead to sin, but alive to God in Christ Jesus
as those who have been brought from death to life
But she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive
We know that we have passed from death to life
Revelation: you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead

rows.alike: Each speaks of being "dead" or of "death", and all but Ephesians 2:1 set it beside "alive" or "life": "was dead and is alive again" (Luke 15:24), "dead in our trespasses" and "made us alive" (Ephesians 2:5), "from death to life" (John 5:24; 1 John 3:14), "alive, yet you are dead" (Revelation 3:1).
rows.different: In Luke 15 one speaks of "this son of mine" and "this brother of yours", adding "He was lost and is found"; Ephesians 2:1 and Colossians 2:13 say "dead in your trespasses"; Romans 6:11 says "dead to sin"; 1 John 3:14 gives "because we love our brothers" and "The one who does not love remains in death"; 1 Timothy 5:6 says "she who lives for pleasure is dead even while she is still alive", and Revelation 3:1 "you have a reputation for being alive, yet you are dead".

rows.title: Fallen asleep

Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 13:3
Give light to my eyes, lest I sleep in death
so a man lies down and does not rise. Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep
The Prophets: then they will fall asleep forever and never wake up
Then they will fall asleep forever and not wake up
Gospels & Acts: The girl is not dead, but asleep
The child is not dead, but asleep
she is not dead but asleep
Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going there to wake him up
They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep, but He was speaking about the death of Lazarus
the bodies of many saints who had fallen asleep were raised
And when he had said this, he fell asleep
The letters: those also who have fallen asleep in Christ
the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep
a number of you have fallen asleep
God will bring with Jesus those who have fallen asleep in Him
Ever since our fathers fell asleep

rows.alike: Each speaks of sleep or of falling asleep: "lest I sleep in death" (Psalm 13:3), "fall asleep forever" (Jeremiah 51:39), "not dead, but asleep" (Matthew 9:24), "he fell asleep" (Acts 7:60), "those who sleep in death" (1 Thessalonians 4:13).
rows.different: Job 14:12 says "Until the heavens are no more, he will not be awakened or roused from sleep", and Jeremiah 51:39 has "I will make them drunk" before "they will fall asleep forever and never wake up"; Jesus says "I am going there to wake him up", and John 11:13 adds "They thought that Jesus was talking about actual sleep"; 1 Corinthians 11:30 has "many among you are weak and sick, and a number of you have fallen asleep"; 1 Thessalonians 4:13 says "those who sleep in death" and "the rest, who are without hope".

rows.title: Gathered to his people; with his fathers

The Law & history: he breathed his last and died, old and contented, and was gathered to his people
Then he breathed his last and died and was gathered to his people, old and full of years
breathed his last, and he was gathered to his people
You will soon rest with your fathers
you will die and be gathered to your people
After that whole generation had also been gathered to their fathers
Then David rested with his fathers and was buried in the City of David
And Solomon rested with his fathers
I will indeed gather you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your grave in peace
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 49:19
he will join the generation of his fathers, who will never see the light of day
Gospels & Acts: His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay
the patriarch David died and was buried, and his tomb is with us to this day

rows.alike: All but Acts 2:29 speak of a death with "people" or "fathers": "gathered to his people" (Genesis 25:8), "gathered to their fathers" (Judges 2:10), "rested with his fathers" (1 Kings 2:10), "join the generation of his fathers" (Psalm 49:19), "buried with his fathers" (Acts 13:36); Acts 2:29 says only that David "died and was buried".
rows.different: Genesis 25:8 and 35:29 add "old and contented" and "old and full of years"; Deuteronomy 32:50 adds "just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people"; 2 Kings 22:20 has "you will be gathered to your grave in peace"; Psalm 49:19 adds "who will never see the light of day"; Acts 13:36 says of David "His body was buried with his fathers and saw decay", and Acts 2:29 "his tomb is with us to this day".

rows.title: Who can praise You from Sheol?

Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 6:5
For there is no mention of You in death; who can praise You from Sheol?
Psalm 30:9
Will the dust praise You? Will it proclaim Your faithfulness?
Psalm 88:10
Do You work wonders for the dead? Do departed spirits rise up to praise You?
Psalm 88:11
Can Your loving devotion be proclaimed in the grave, Your faithfulness in Abaddon?
Psalm 115:17
It is not the dead who praise the LORD, nor any who descend into silence
Ecclesiastes 9:5
For the living know that they will die, but the dead know nothing
Ecclesiastes 9:10
for in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom
The Prophets: For Sheol cannot thank You; Death cannot praise You. Those who descend to the Pit cannot hope for Your faithfulness
The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today

rows.alike: Most ask whether the dead praise, or say they do not: "who can praise You from Sheol?" (Psalm 6:5), "It is not the dead who praise the LORD" (Psalm 115:17), "Death cannot praise You" (Isaiah 38:18); "Your faithfulness" is named in Psalm 30:9, Psalm 88:11 and Isaiah 38:18 and 38:19.
rows.different: Psalm 30:9 has "my descent to the Pit" and Psalm 115:17 "nor any who descend into silence"; Isaiah 38:19 says "The living, only the living, can thank You, as I do today"; Ecclesiastes does not mention praise: "the dead know nothing", and "in Sheol, where you are going, there is no work or planning or knowledge or wisdom".

rows.title: Scattered among the nations

The Law & history: But I will scatter you among the nations
Then the LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and only a few of you will survive among the nations
Then the LORD will scatter you among all the nations, from one end of the earth to the other
The LORD will bring you and the king you appoint to a nation neither you nor your fathers have known
If you are unfaithful, I will scatter you among the nations
There is a certain people scattered and dispersed among the peoples of every province of your kingdom
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 44:11
You have scattered us among the nations
Psalm 106:27
to disperse their offspring among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands
The Prophets: I will scatter them among the nations that neither they nor their fathers have known
So I will cast you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known
when I disperse them among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries
I would scatter them among the nations and disperse them throughout the lands
I will disperse you among the nations and scatter you throughout the lands
I dispersed them among the nations, and they were scattered throughout the lands
And I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the countries
you are scattered among the nations and throughout the lands
I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands
I will disperse the Egyptians among the nations and scatter them throughout the lands
Gospels & Acts: where the Jews are dispersed among the Greeks

rows.alike: The same words recur, "scatter" and "disperse" "among the nations": "I will scatter you among the nations" (Leviticus 26:33; Nehemiah 1:8), "You have scattered us among the nations" (Psalm 44:11), "I dispersed them among the nations" (Ezekiel 36:19), "when you are scattered among the nations" (Ezekiel 6:8); and "neither you nor your fathers have known" (Deuteronomy 28:36; Jeremiah 16:13), "neither they nor their fathers have known" (Jeremiah 9:16).
rows.different: Leviticus 26:33 has "I will scatter you", Deuteronomy 4:27 "the LORD will scatter you among the peoples, and only a few of you will survive"; Nehemiah 1:8 recalls "the word that You commanded Your servant Moses"; Psalm 44:11 says "You have given us up as sheep to be devoured"; Esther 3:8 is Haman's word to the king; Ezekiel 29:12, 30:23 and 30:26 are said of "the Egyptians"; John 7:35 is what "the Jews said to one another" of "Him": "Where does He intend to go that we will not find Him?"

rows.title: Wanderers among the nations, with no place to rest

The Law & history: You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth
from Your face I will be hidden; I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth
He made them wander in the wilderness forty years, until the whole generation who had done evil in His sight was gone
Among those nations you will find no repose, not even a resting place for the sole of your foot
But the dove found no place to rest her foot
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 109:10
May his children wander as beggars
The Prophets: My God will reject them because they have not obeyed Him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations
she dwells among the nations but finds no place to rest
The letters: They wandered in deserts and mountains

rows.alike: Each speaks of wandering or of finding no rest, apart from the two cells marked aside: "a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth" (Genesis 4:12), "wanderers among the nations" (Hosea 9:17), "no repose, not even a resting place" among the nations (Deuteronomy 28:65), "finds no place to rest" (Lamentations 1:3).
rows.different: Genesis 4:12 and 4:14 have "from Your face I will be hidden" and "whoever finds me will kill me"; Numbers 32:13 says "He made them wander in the wilderness forty years"; Psalm 109:10 wishes it on "his children"; Lamentations 1:3 tells it as having happened, "Judah has gone into exile", and 4:15 adds "They can stay here no longer". Genesis 8:9 (the dove) and Hebrews 11:38 ("The world was not worthy of them") use the words of another subject.

rows.title: Cast out of His presence

The Law & history: and He removed them from His presence
until He had banished them from His presence
I will remove Judah from My sight, just as I removed Israel
until He finally banished them from His presence
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 51:11
Cast me not away from Your presence
The Prophets: And I will cast you out of My presence, just as I have cast out all your brothers
I will surely forget you and will cast you out of My presence
until He finally banished them from His presence

rows.alike: The same words, being removed or cast out of the LORD's presence: "He removed them from His presence" (2 Kings 17:18), "He finally banished them from His presence" (2 Kings 24:20; Jeremiah 52:3), "I will cast you out of My presence" (Jeremiah 7:15), "Cast me not away from Your presence" (Psalm 51:11).
rows.different: Kings tells it of Israel and then Judah, "just as I removed Israel"; 2 Kings 24:20 and Jeremiah 52:3 are word for word the same; Jeremiah 7:15 adds "just as I have cast out all your brothers, all the descendants of Ephraim", and 23:39 "I will surely forget you"; Psalm 51:11 is a request, "Cast me not away from Your presence; take not Your Holy Spirit from me".

rows.title: Into exile for their unfaithfulness

The Law & history: All this happened because the people of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God
But they were unfaithful to the God of their fathers
But Judah was exiled to Babylon because of their unfaithfulness
Because of our iniquities, we and our kings and priests have been delivered into the hands of the kings of the earth and subjected to the sword and to captivity
The Prophets: the house of Israel went into exile for their iniquity, because they were unfaithful to Me
in all the countries to which You have driven us because of our unfaithfulness to You
For the LORD has brought her grief because of her many transgressions. Her children have gone away as captives before the enemy

rows.alike: Each speaks of unfaithfulness, iniquity or sin, mostly with "because": "because of their unfaithfulness" (1 Chronicles 9:1), "because they were unfaithful to Me" (Ezekiel 39:23), "because of our unfaithfulness to You" (Daniel 9:7), "Because of our iniquities" (Ezra 9:7), "because of her many transgressions" (Lamentations 1:5), "because the people of Israel had sinned against the LORD their God" (2 Kings 17:7).
rows.different: Kings and Chronicles say "All this happened" (2 Kings 17:7) and "Judah was exiled to Babylon" (1 Chronicles 9:1); Ezra 9:7 and Daniel 9:7 say "we" and "our"; Ezekiel 39:23 gives it as what "the nations will know"; Lamentations 1:5 says "the LORD has brought her grief" and "Her children have gone away as captives before the enemy".

rows.title: Carried away into exile, away from its own land

The Law & history: carried away the Israelites to Assyria
So Israel was exiled from their homeland into Assyria, where they are to this day
to take the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh into exile
He took them into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon
So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land
the exiles carried away to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar its king
carried away the people to Babylon
He had been carried into exile from Jerusalem by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon
The Prophets: So Judah was taken into exile, away from its own land
to all the exiles who were carried away from Jerusalem to Babylon
After Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried away Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah
and Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland
And Israel will surely go into exile, away from their homeland
carried Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim king of Judah into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon
Nebuchadnezzar had carried into exile from Jerusalem to Babylon
all you exiles I have sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon
your sons have been taken into exile
Gospels & Acts: at the time of the exile to Babylon
fourteen from David to the exile to Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to the Christ

rows.alike: The same words, "into exile" and "carried away", with the places named: "to Assyria" (2 Kings 17:6), "to Babylon" (2 Kings 24:15; Jeremiah 27:20; 29:1; 29:4), and "away from its own land" (2 Kings 25:21; Jeremiah 52:27), "away from their homeland" (Amos 7:11).
rows.different: Amos says it beforehand, "Israel will surely go into exile"; Kings, Chronicles, Ezra and Esther tell it after; 2 Kings 25:21 and Jeremiah 52:27 are word for word the same; Matthew uses "the exile to Babylon" to mark the generations; Jeremiah 48:46 says it of Moab, "your sons have been taken into exile".

rows.title: By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept

The Law & history: When I heard these words, I sat down and wept
Now I assembled these exiles at the canal that flows to Ahava
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 137:1
By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept when we remembered Zion
Psalm 137:4
How can we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land?
The Prophets: while I was among the exiles by the River Kebar
I came to the exiles at Tel-abib who dwelt by the River Kebar. And for seven days I sat where they sat

rows.alike: Most speak of exiles by water or of sitting in grief: "By the rivers of Babylon we sat and wept" (Psalm 137:1), "among the exiles by the River Kebar" (Ezekiel 1:1), "I sat where they sat" (Ezekiel 3:15), "I sat down and wept" (Nehemiah 1:4), "these exiles at the canal that flows to Ahava" (Ezra 8:15).
rows.different: Psalm 137:1 adds "when we remembered Zion", and 137:4 asks "How can we sing a song of the LORD in a foreign land?"; Ezekiel 1:1 has "I saw visions of God" while "among the exiles by the River Kebar"; Nehemiah 1:4 weeps "When I heard these words" and "mourned for days, fasting and praying"; Ezra 8:15 has "we camped there three days".

rows.title: I will hide My face; your sins have hidden His face

The Law & history: I will abandon them and hide My face from them
I will surely hide My face because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods
I will hide My face from them; I will see what will be their end
Psalms & wisdom: Psalm 51:9
Hide Your face from my sins and blot out all my iniquities
The Prophets: But your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God, and your sins have hidden His face from you, so that He does not hear
Your iniquities have diverted these from you; your sins have deprived you of My bounty
I was enraged by his sinful greed, so I struck him and hid My face in anger
I have hidden My face from this city because of all its wickedness
I dealt with them according to their uncleanness and transgressions, and I hid My face from them
At that time He will hide His face from them because of the evil they have done
In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment
And I will no longer hide My face from them
I did not hide My face from scorn and spittle

rows.alike: Most speak of the LORD hiding His face, and several tie it to sin: "because of all the evil they have done by turning to other gods" (Deuteronomy 31:18), "because of the evil they have done" (Micah 3:4), "because of all its wickedness" (Jeremiah 33:5), "your sins have hidden His face from you" (Isaiah 59:2).
rows.different: Most are the LORD speaking, "I will hide My face"; Isaiah 59:2 has "your iniquities have built barriers between you and your God"; Jeremiah 5:25 does not mention a face: "your sins have deprived you of My bounty"; in Psalm 51:9 the speaker asks God to hide His face "from my sins"; Isaiah 54:8 says "In a surge of anger I hid My face from you for a moment" and Ezekiel 39:29 "I will no longer hide My face from them". Isaiah 50:6 uses the words of another subject: "I did not hide My face from scorn and spittle".

rows.title: He gave them over

The Law & history: He delivered them into the hands of those who plundered them
So You delivered them into the hands of enemies who oppressed them
Yet they would not listen, so You gave them into the hands of the neighboring peoples
Psalms & wisdom: Job 8:4
When your children sinned against Him, He gave them over to their rebellion
Psalm 81:12
So I gave them up to their stubborn hearts to follow their own devices
Psalm 106:41
He delivered them into the hand of the nations
The Prophets: I also gave them over to statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live
The letters: Therefore God gave them over in the desires of their hearts to impurity
For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions
He gave them up to a depraved mind

rows.alike: The same words of God handing people over: "He gave them over to their rebellion" (Job 8:4), "I gave them up to their stubborn hearts" (Psalm 81:12), "God gave them over in the desires of their hearts" (Romans 1:24), and into enemies' hands, "He delivered them into the hand of the nations" (Psalm 106:41).
rows.different: Judges 2:14, Nehemiah 9:27 and 9:30 and Psalm 106:41 speak of being given into the hands of enemies and nations; Job 8:4 says "When your children sinned against Him"; Psalm 81:12 is in the first person, "I gave them up"; Ezekiel 20:25 has "statutes that were not good and ordinances by which they could not live"; Romans 1:24, 26 and 28 say it three times, and 1:28 gives "since they did not see fit to acknowledge God".

rows.title: The iniquity of the fathers on the children

The Law & history: visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me
visiting the iniquity of the fathers on their children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me
He will visit the iniquity of the fathers on their children and grandchildren to the third and fourth generations
He will visit the iniquity of the fathers upon their children to the third and fourth generation
The Prophets: but lay the iniquity of the fathers into the laps of their children after them
Our fathers sinned and are no more, but we bear their punishment

rows.alike: The same words, "the iniquity of the fathers" and "their children" (Exodus 20:5; Deuteronomy 5:9; Exodus 34:7; Numbers 14:18; Jeremiah 32:18), and in Lamentations "Our fathers sinned ... we bear their punishment".
rows.different: Exodus 20:5 and Deuteronomy 5:9 follow "You shall not bow down to them or worship them" and add "of those who hate Me"; Exodus 34:7 and Numbers 14:18 follow "forgiving iniquity" and continue "Yet He will by no means leave the guilty unpunished"; Exodus 34:7 adds "and grandchildren"; Jeremiah 32:18 says "You show loving devotion to thousands but lay the iniquity of the fathers into the laps of their children after them"; Lamentations 5:7 speaks as "we", of "Our fathers" who "are no more".
